CDN delivery is disabled, but the local CSS/JS files are not present in %s. TYPO3 drops missing files from includeCSS/includeJS without an error, so the frontend may render unstyled. Run the console command "t3sbootstrap:cdnToLocal" (or the scheduler task) to fetch them.

SCSS is enabled, but the Bootstrap sources are not present in %sT3SB-Bootstrap/Bootstrap/scss/. They are a download and cannot be rebuilt from the configuration record, and a directory below typo3temp/ is cleared by every TYPO3 update, deployment or cache flush. Without them the stylesheet reference points at nothing, TYPO3 drops it without an error and the page renders unstyled. Note that the include file Bootstrap/bootstrap-<uid>.scss is not rebuilt from the configuration record either - only the command writes it. Run the console command "t3sbootstrap:customScss <root page id>" (or the scheduler task "T3SB Custom SCSS").
Back up and transfer the configuration

Saves the t3sbootstrap configuration of a site root as a portable JSON file - as the backup of this installation, or to import it into another one. The export contains no uid and no pid, so the target page tree may look completely different. It holds everything a setup consists of: the configuration record with the own scss (variables and overrides), the extension configuration, and the site's t3sbootstrap sets together with their settings - Bootstrap version, Bootswatch and Google Fonts among them. To step back through single changes instead, use the record history of the configuration record.
You are not allowed to access the configuration of that page.
Update - keep the existing record and its uid
Replace - delete the existing record and create a new one
Add - only when the target page has no configuration yet

TYPO3 %s on PHP %s. Besides the configuration record the export carries the extension configuration, the sets and settings of this site, and the inventory below - so the target installation can tell what it is missing. Only the t3sbootstrap sets are imported there, the others are listed for reference.

config/system/settings.php is not writable here. The export works regardless - this only matters for an import into this installation.
The %s sets of this site, read from config/sites/%s/config.yaml.
This page belongs to no site, so there are no sets to read.

They are maintained in Site Management, Sites, tab Sets. The import adds only the ones marked t3sbootstrap - the others are listed because a site configuration becomes invalid as soon as one of its sets is missing on the target, and that is easier to see here than there.

The export names all %s extensions installed here with their composer name and version - core packages excluded, those follow from the TYPO3 version. None of it is ever imported, an extension cannot install another one. The list is meant for the target installation: its preview compares it against what is installed there and names what is missing, with the matching composer require line. It is also the record of the environment this setup ran in.

The %s values with the prefix bootstrap. from the settings.yaml of this site - only those that differ from the defaults of the sets. These are written on the target, every other extension's settings there stay untouched.
This site has no own t3sbootstrap settings - everything is on the defaults of the sets.

The %s values from EXTENSIONS.t3sbootstrap in config/system/settings.php, maintained in the install tool. The two paths assetDir and flexformDir are missing on purpose - they belong to the host and are never written on a target.
The same export as a file, for a scheduler task that keeps a regular backup, or for a deployment script:
Update is the normal case: the existing record is overwritten and keeps its uid. Fields the import does not carry are reset to their default value, so the result matches the export exactly.
Replace deletes the existing record and creates a new one. Its uid changes, and the old one stays behind as a deleted record. Rarely necessary.

Add only imports when the target page has no configuration at all. If there already is one, the import stops with a message and changes nothing - the safe choice when you are not sure what is on the target page.
uid of the configuration record this block belongs to
Pixel width of the navbar breakpoint, derived from the chosen breakpoint

Written to config/system/settings.php (the block EXTENSIONS.t3sbootstrap) and to the config/sites/ folder of the site the target page selected above belongs to - config.yaml for the sets, settings.yaml for the settings.
Nothing is written right away. First comes a preview with every value that would change, old and new side by side, and only a second confirmation writes it.

Only what belongs to t3sbootstrap is touched: sets with the prefix t3sbs/t3sbootstrap and settings with the prefix bootstrap. The settings of every other extension in the same settings.yaml stay exactly as they are.
The two paths assetDir and flexformDir are never imported. They belong to this host, and overwriting the asset directory leaves the site without styling.
Both files usually live in version control, so a write here lasts until the next deployment. If they are not writable, the preview offers the finished lines to paste instead.
